checks: Source 43892fde2d187dd5 §§4 and 7 uses the same raw John objective, harmonic interpolation, endpoint deletion, complementary reflection, and cube sharpness.

Positive-mass feasible bases are exactly the base hull lattice points: one can realize a convex representation by sufficiently small constant-density allocations. The zero pair alone does not qualify. Closedness of the moment graph gives upper semicontinuity of the John radius by taking limits of uniformly bounded ellipsoids.

At a positive anchor, adding any slack on its own fiber leaves the centered base moment zero, contradicting maximal mass. The homothetic deletion sources have their claimed mass and a raw moment inball. Adding its reflection strictly improves the radius, including if the original section has dimension below d.

For a nontrivial integer convex combination of maximizing bases, the harmonic t and weights α_i sum correctly and produce the raw pair (t,tj). Strict interpolation contradicts joint optimality. Midpoints exclude repeated parity, and the n=0 singleton convention is valid.

On the binary product the feasible integer bases are extreme, so all balanced sources use only their own identical fiber. Complementation is a bijection of sources, reflects the raw moment bodies, and fixes the unique real maximizing pair. For the symmetric moment body, an off-center ellipsoid gives a strictly larger one by adding the nonzero rank-one shape increment.
